exposure: newborn birthweight from or above 4,000 g
cohort: The study included 18,917 women who gave birth in Surinamese hospitals in 2020 and 2021, with pregnancies >= 27 weeks of gestation.
finding: The overall facility-based CS rate in Suriname was 23.9%, with previous CS, BMI > 40, and newborn birthweight >= 4,000g being significant risk factors.
mod_finding: Robson group 5 (multiparous women with a previous CS and a singleton term cephalic pregnancy) contributed the largest proportion (30.5%) to the overall CS rate.
birth_weight: N/A (birthweight from or above 4,000g was an exposure/risk factor, not a cohort inclusion criteria for all infants)
